subproblem.title: The upper n-density ratio limsup of an arbitrary measure is Borel measurable (supplied proof, step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). For x ∈ ℝ^P let Θ*(x) := limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n), the limsup taken in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>]0, where B_ρ(x) is the open ball and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n (the quotient is ENNReal division by ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)). Then x ↦ Θ*(x).toReal is Borel measurable on ℝ^P. No finiteness assumption on μ is made.

Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 1 of that proof ("Measurability of dens μ, any measure μ"). Its lower semicontinuity claim is proved here by continuity from below instead of Fatou's lemma; both give the same fact.
Notation: c_ρ := ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ∈ [0, ∞] and g_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x))/c_ρ for ρ ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P, so Θ*(x) = limsup_{𝓝[>]0} (ρ ↦ g_ρ(x)).
1. (0 < ω_n < ∞.) ω_n = volume(B_1(0)) with B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n. The volume on the finite-dimensional inner product space Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, so it is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on bounded sets. Hence ω_n ∈ (0, ∞). This includes n = 0, where Euclid 0 = {0} and B_1(0) = {0} is open and nonempty. Consequently, for ρ > 0, ρ^n > 0 and c_ρ ∈ (0, ∞).
2. (Lower semicontinuity of balls.) Fix ρ > 0. Then h_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x)) ∈ [0, ∞] is lower semicontinuous in x. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and t < h_ρ(x). The open balls B_{s_m}(x) with s_m := ρ(1 − 1/(m+2)) increase with m, and their union is B_ρ(x). By continuity from below, μ(B_ρ(x)) = sup_m μ(B_{s_m}(x)) (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop for the monotone family), so t < μ(B_{s_m}(x)) for some m. If |x' − x| < ρ − s_m, then B_{s_m}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x') (|z − x'| ≤ |z − x| + |x − x'| < s_m + (ρ − s_m)), so t < μ(B_ρ(x')). Hence {x' : t < h_ρ(x')} is a neighbourhood of x. This is lower semicontinuity.
3. (Rescaled balls.) For ρ > 0, g_ρ = h_ρ·c_ρ⁻¹ with the constant c_ρ⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞). Multiplication by a finite constant is a continuous monotone self-map of [0, ∞], so it preserves lower semicontinuity (Continuous.comp_lowerSemicontinuous with a monotone outer map; ENNReal.continuous_div_const needs only c_ρ ≠ 0). Hence g_ρ is lower semicontinuous for every ρ > 0.
4. (Truncated suprema.) For ε > 0 let G_ε(x) := sup_{ρ ∈ (0, ε)} g_ρ(x). A pointwise supremum of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous (lowerSemicontinuous_iSup / lowerSemicontinuous_biSup), so each G_ε is lower semicontinuous. Each set {G_ε > t} is then open, so G_ε is Borel measurable (LowerSemicontinuous.measurable). Only ρ > 0 enters G_ε.
5. (limsup as a countable infimum.) The intervals (0, ε), ε > 0, form a basis of 𝓝[>]0. By Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup, Θ*(x) = inf_{ε>0} G_ε(x). G_ε(x) is non-decreasing in ε. Each 1/(m+1) is positive, so inf_{ε>0} G_ε(x) ≤ inf_{m∈ℕ} G_{1/(m+1)}(x). Conversely, for every ε > 0 there is m with 1/(m+1) < ε, and then G_{1/(m+1)}(x) ≤ G_ε(x). Hence Θ*(x) = inf_{m∈ℕ} G_{1/(m+1)}(x). Equivalently, apply the basis lemma to a countable basis of 𝓝[>]0 indexed by m ∈ ℕ, e.g. the sets B_{1/(m+1)}(0) ∩ (0, ∞) (nhdsWithin_hasBasis Metric.nhds_basis_ball_inv_nat_succ).
6. (Conclusion.) x ↦ Θ*(x) is a countable infimum of the Borel functions G_{1/(m+1)} (step 4), so it is Borel measurable (Measurable.iInf). ENNReal.toReal is measurable (ENNReal.measurable_toReal), so x ↦ Θ*(x).toReal is Borel measurable. ∎

x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous by continuity from below on the balls B_{s}(x), s ↑ ρ.
Dividing by c_ρ and taking suprema over ρ ∈ (0, ε) preserves lower semicontinuity, so G_ε is Borel.
limsup along 𝓝[>]0 equals inf_m G_{1/(m+1)}, a countable infimum; toReal is measurable.

subproblem.title: Normalization μHE[n] = a·μH[n]: local integrability of g·e and ∫ f(g·e) dμH[n] = (c∫f dμ)·e for μ = Hⁿ⌞g (supplied proof, steps 2 and 5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. There is a real constant c > 0 with the following property. Let Q ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel measurable with g ≥ 0, and let e ∈ ℝ^Q. Assume μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K and μ = μHE[n].withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(g(x))). Then (i) x ↦ g(x)e is locally integrable with respect to the Hausdorff measure μH[n] on ℝ^P; and (ii) for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f(x)·(g(x)e) dμH[n](x) = (c·∫ f dμ)·e.

Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 2 of that proof ("Normalization": (a), (b), (c)) together with the local integrability part of step 5 ((H1)).
1. (The constant.) By euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, on every Euclid P, μHE[n] = a•μH[n] with a := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on Euclid n, μH[n] on Euclid n) ∈ ℝ≥0. a depends only on n. By addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero, a ≠ 0, and a < ∞ because a ∈ ℝ≥0. Put c := (a : ℝ)⁻¹ > 0. Fix Q, μ, g, e satisfying the hypotheses.
2. (Lower integrals.) For a Borel set A and a Borel h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_A h dμHE[n] = a·∫⁻_A h dμH[n] (Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure). By withDensity_apply, μ(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμHE[n] = a·∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμH[n]. Since a ∈ (0, ∞), ∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμH[n] = a⁻¹·μ(A).
3. ((i) local integrability.) g is Borel, so x ↦ g(x)•e is Borel (Measurable.smul_const). Euclid Q is second countable, so this map is strongly measurable and in particular a.e. strongly measurable for μH[n]. Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and use the neighbourhood B_1(x) ∈ 𝓝 x. Since g ≥ 0, ‖g(z)•e‖ₑ = ofReal(g(z))·‖e‖ₑ. Step 2 gives ∫⁻_{B_1(x)} ‖g•e‖ₑ dμH[n] = ‖e‖ₑ·a⁻¹·μ(B_1(x)) ≤ ‖e‖ₑ·a⁻¹·μ(closedBall x 1) < ∞, because closedBall x 1 is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and μ is finite on compact sets. So g•e is integrable on a neighbourhood of every point, i.e. LocallyIntegrable (g•e) μH[n]. Equivalently, by locallyIntegrable_iff it suffices that g•e be integrable on every compact K; the same computation with K in place of B_1(x) bounds the lower integral (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal), and Integrable.smul_const handles e.
4. ((ii), pulling out e.) Fix f. f(x)•(g(x)•e) = (f(x)g(x))•e (smul_smul), and integral_smul_const gives ∫ f(x)•(g(x)•e) dμH[n] = (∫ f g dμH[n])•e. This holds whether or not f g is μH[n]-integrable. If it is not and e ≠ 0, then x ↦ (f(x)g(x))•e is not integrable either, so both sides are 0. If e = 0, both sides are 0.
5. (From μH[n] to μHE[n].) integral_smul_nnreal_measure (or integral_smul_measure with the coercion of a) gives ∫ f g dμHE[n] = ∫ f g d(a•μH[n]) = a·∫ f g dμH[n]. Since a ≠ 0, ∫ f g dμH[n] = a⁻¹·∫ f g dμHE[n].
6. (From μHE[n] to μ.) ofReal(g(x)) = ((g x).toNNReal : [0, ∞]) by definition of ENNReal.ofReal, and x ↦ (g x).toNNReal is measurable. integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul gives ∫ f dμ = ∫ f d(μHE[n].withDensity(x ↦ (g x).toNNReal)) = ∫ (g x).toNNReal • f(x) dμHE[n] = ∫ g f dμHE[n], using ((g x).toNNReal : ℝ) = g(x) since g ≥ 0. This identity is unconditional.
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 4–6 give ∫ f(x)•(g(x)•e) dμH[n] = (a⁻¹·∫ f dμ)•e = (c·∫ f dμ)•e. Steps 3 and 7 prove (i) and (ii) with the constant c of step 1, which depends only on n. ∎

subproblem.title: Support semicontinuity under vague convergence with a uniform lower mass bound on exhausting domains (supplied proof, step 8; (T3s))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ, let μ and μ_k (k ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^P, U ⊆ ℝ^P, D_k ⊆ ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ), y_k, y ∈ ℝ^P. Write spt ν := {z : ν(B_ε(z)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0}. Assume: every μ_k is finite on compact sets; U is open; every compact K ⊆ U satisfies K ⊆ D_k for all sufficiently large k; for every k, every z ∈ spt μ_k and every ρ > 0 with closedBall z ρ ⊆ D_k, ofReal(e^{−Λρ})·ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n) ≤ μ_k(B_ρ(z)) (ω_n = unitBallVolume n); ∫ f dμ_k → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ; y_k ∈ spt μ_k for every k; y_k → y and y ∈ U. Then y ∈ spt μ, i.e. μ(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.

This child is step 8 of that proof (support semicontinuity, the parent's (T3s)), stated for an arbitrary sequence of measures, with the domains D(μ_k) written as D_k and D(μ) as U.
1. (The lower bound is positive and finite.) For r > 0 put m(r) := ofReal(e^{−Λr})·(ω_n·ofReal(r^n)). e^{−Λr} > 0 and r^n > 0. ω_n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n) ∈ (0, ∞), since the Haar volume of a nonempty open bounded set is positive and finite (n = 0 included). Hence m(r) ∈ (0, ∞) and m(r).toReal > 0.
2. (A compact neighbourhood inside the domains.) U is open and y ∈ U, so choose r₀ > 0 with B_{r₀}(y) ⊆ U and set ρ₁ := r₀/4. Then K₀ := closedBall y (2ρ₁) ⊆ B_{r₀}(y) ⊆ U, and K₀ is compact (ℝ^P is proper). By hypothesis there is k₁ with K₀ ⊆ D_k for all k ≥ k₁.
3. (Reduction.) Fix ε > 0 and let ε' := min(ε, ρ₁) > 0. Since B_{ε'}(y) ⊆ B_ε(y), μ(B_{ε'}(y)) ≤ μ(B_ε(y)), so it suffices to prove μ(B_{ε'}(y)) ≠ 0.
4. (A bump function.) Choose f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support such that 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on closedBall y (ε'/2), and tsupport f ⊆ closedBall y (3ε'/4) ⊆ B_{ε'}(y). For example, take a ContDiffBump centred at y with rIn = ε'/2 < rOut = 3ε'/4: it equals 1 on closedBall y rIn, takes values in [0, 1], and its tsupport is closedBall y rOut. Alternatively take f(x) = min(1, max(0, (3ε'/4 − |x − y|)/(ε'/4))).
5. (Large k.) Since y_k → y there is k₂ with |y_k − y| < ε'/4 for k ≥ k₂. Let k ≥ max(k₁, k₂). (a) closedBall y_k (ε'/4) ⊆ closedBall y (ε'/2) ⊆ closedBall y (2ρ₁) = K₀ ⊆ D_k, using ε' ≤ ρ₁. (b) B_{ε'/4}(y_k) ⊆ B_{ε'/2}(y) ⊆ {f = 1}. By (a), y_k ∈ spt μ_k and the lower-bound hypothesis at radius ρ = ε'/4 > 0, m(ε'/4) ≤ μ_k(B_{ε'/4}(y_k)).
6. (Integral lower bound.) f is μ_k-integrable: it is continuous with compact support, and μ_k is finite on the compact set tsupport f (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport with the IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts instance built from the hypothesis). By (b) and f ≥ 0, 0 ≤ 1_{B_{ε'/4}(y_k)} ≤ f pointwise. Also μ_k(B_{ε'/4}(y_k)) ≤ μ_k(tsupport f) < ∞, so the indicator is integrable. Hence ∫ f dμ_k ≥ ∫ 1_{B_{ε'/4}(y_k)} dμ_k = μ_k(B_{ε'/4}(y_k)).toReal ≥ m(ε'/4).toReal =: m₀ > 0. The last inequality uses step 5, toReal monotone on finite values, and m(ε'/4) < ∞. Equivalently, ∫ f dμ_k ≥ ∫_{B_{ε'/4}(y_k)} f dμ_k (setIntegral_le_integral, f ≥ 0) and that set integral equals μ_k(B_{ε'/4}(y_k)).toReal (setIntegral_congr_fun with f = 1 there). This holds for all k ≥ max(k₁, k₂).
7. (Passing to the limit.) By vague convergence, ∫ f dμ_k → ∫ f dμ. Since ∫ f dμ_k ≥ m₀ eventually, ∫ f dμ ≥ m₀ > 0 (ge_of_tendsto).
8. (Conclusion.) Suppose μ(B_{ε'}(y)) = 0. The set {f ≠ 0} is contained in tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε'}(y), so f = 0 μ-almost everywhere and ∫ f dμ = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae). This contradicts step 7. Hence μ(B_{ε'}(y)) ≠ 0, and by step 3 μ(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, y ∈ spt μ. No finiteness of μ is needed. ∎

The lower mass bound at y_k ∈ spt μ_k gives ∫ f dμ_k ≥ μ_k(B_{ε'/4}(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λε'/4}ω_n(ε'/4)^n > 0 for a bump f = 1 on closedBall y (ε'/2), supported in B_{ε'}(y).
Vague convergence gives ∫ f dμ > 0, which is impossible if μ(B_{ε'}(y)) = 0; monotonicity in ε finishes.
